turns.assessment: The simultaneous brief client errors, och129 line-interface errored seconds, and immediate protection switch/revert at t=600 indicate a short impairment of shared lightpath och129. A fast SOP transient on the S08–S24 fibre route best fits because it can cause errored seconds without a sampled power, OSNR, BER, DGD, or amplifier change. The evidence does not identify which span was disturbed, while persistent optical faults and hard card failures are contradicted by unchanged monitoring; therefore no element-specific repair reaches 80% confidence.

proposals.rationale: A millisecond-scale polarization transient on the S08-to-S24 path can produce the observed brief och129 and client errored seconds and protection switch/revert while escaping sampled optical telemetry. The reverse-end errors are also compatible with disturbance of both fibres in the same cable.
Handling of a shared span could briefly disturb och129, but this mode predicts a power excursion; no channel-power, receiver-power, or amplifier-power change was recorded.

A transient interruption at the S24 OTN switch could affect the multiple ODUs carried on och129 without an optical signature, but a documented hard switch-fabric failure would normally affect additional ODUs and persist.
